thread:
jules: Seeing a wave of 502/504s in us-west-2 edge yesterday evening. ALB metrics show lots of 'connection reset by peer' and nodes reporting 'connect: cannot assign requested address'.

maria: Confirmed. Egress errors spiking from model-puller pods, and ecr pulls failing intermittently. tcpdump shows tons of SYNs in TIME_WAIT.

sam: Looks like ephemeral port reuse / conntrack exhaustion. conntrack count near 260k on a node and ip_local_port_range is default 32768-60999.

jules: Cloudwatch for NAT GW in the affected AZ shows simultaneous connections near the soft limit; NAT metrics: ActiveConnections spiked and SNAT port exhaustion alarms fired.

maria: Oncall-bot alerted at 20:12 with 15% of requests failing. Rolling restart reduced errors briefly but they came back.

devops: Short term mitigation: we added a second NAT GW in the same AZ and moved some Egress routes -> reduced error rate to ~2%.

sam: Long term: we should __reduce egress churn__. Action items: 1) add VPC endpoints for ECR/S3 in all clusters 2) enable HTTP keepalive and reuse connection pools for model pulls 3) add NLB with static IPs for cross-AZ egress balancing 4) tune conntrack and ephemeral port range.

maria: For conntrack/port tuning notes:
```
# increase ephemeral port range
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535'
# increase conntrack max
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1000000
# verify current
cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
```

jules: Also consider an internal egress proxy (nginx/traefik with keepalive) to terminate many short-lived outbound connections. That reduces SNAT churn.

devops: Proposing a follow-up: create a runbook with detection signals (conntrack > 80%, NAT ActiveConnections > 70%, increase in TIME_WAIT) and automated scaling to add extra NAT gateway or route table fallback to another AZ's NAT.

sam: I'll open a ticket to add VPC endpoints and proxy work, plus a patch to model-puller to enable persistent connections. Assign to infra-edges.

maria: QA: also verify kube-proxy mode and node-local dns, since weird iptables rules can increase conn churn.

oncall-bot: Incident closed — monitoring alerts now green. Please keep an eye on spikes; runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-nat-port.json :thumbsup:

jules: Thanks all. Logged follow-ups in BOARD-432 and infra-edges backlog.
